sector_model: Company-operated restaurants: P/E, FCF after growth capex, net cash, operating lease obligations tracked separately from debt, buybacks vs FCF.
thesis: Chipotle (NYSE: CMG), company-operated fast-casual chain. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-10-29) read. Q3 revenue 3,293M (+9.7%), comparable sales +2.1% (check +1.3%, transactions +0.8%); but Q3 operating income 452M vs 477M and net income 340M vs 382M (-11%); 9M operating margin 14.1% vs 16.9%. Management cites low-single-digit comps headwinds from July. 9M OCF 1,922M, capex 641M (up from 469M); buybacks 1,465M in 9M, only 118M in Q3 at average 34.05 (vs 42.39 a year ago). No financial debt; cash and investments 1,003M. Close 35.55 (2026-11-20) x 1,264,975k shares (cover, 2026-10-26) = 44.97B = 32.7x TTM NI 1,377M; TTM FCF 1,510M (3.4%). Quality business with net cash; price assumes margin recovery and unit growth, with margins and comps currently moving the wrong way.
counterthesis: Margins are falling (labor, occupancy, other costs growing faster than sales; G&A +26% in Q3), comps are only +2.1% on mostly price, and the shares still trade at 32.7x TTM earnings and about 3.4% FCF yield. Buybacks cut sharply in Q3, so per-share support has weakened. Operating leases of 5.6B are real fixed obligations. 2026 capex up 36% on new units and equipment (elevated through 2027 per filing).
invalidation: Downgrade if comps turn negative or restaurant-level margin keeps falling; upgrade case needs stabilized margins at a lower multiple, verified peers (MCD, SBUX, CAVA, WING) and verified quotes.
